title: Northern Serengeti and the Mara River
excerpt: The northern Serengeti, around Kogatende and the Mara River, is where the river crossings of the Great Migration happen. When to go and what to expect.
body:
The northern Serengeti is a quieter, hilly region close to the Kenyan border. For a few months a year, it is the stage for one of the most dramatic wildlife events in the world.

## The Mara River crossings

From roughly July to October, large herds of wildebeest and zebra move between the Serengeti and Kenya's Masai Mara. To do so, they cross the Mara River, where crocodiles wait. Crossings can happen several times a day, or not for days. Read more about [river crossings](/blog/great-migration-river-crossings/).

## The landscape

Rolling hills, open grassland and woodland along the rivers. Fewer roads and lodges than in the central area, which gives it a wild feel.

## Outside the migration months

Even without the herds, the north is beautiful. Resident lions, elephants, giraffes and buffaloes live here, and you will see very few other vehicles.

## Getting there

From central Serengeti it is a long drive (half a day or more). Many travellers fly to the Kogatende airstrip. See [fly-in safaris](/blog/fly-in-safari/).

## Where to stay

Mobile and permanent tented camps near the river. Book early for the migration season. See [where to stay for the migration](/blog/migration-camps-where-to-stay/).
